overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 4
overview.text: In this lesson, students develop a deep conceptual and procedural understanding of Why Do Banks Pay YOU to Provide Their Services? in Module 3: Linear and Exponential Functions.
outcomes: Students compare the rate of change for simple and compound interest and recognize situations in which a quantity grows by a constant percent rate per unit interval.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize precise mathematical definitions and multiple problem-solving representations. Encourage students to check the reasonableness of their numerical solutions.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 4 Exit Ticket: Why Do Banks Pay YOU to Provide Their Services?
exitTicket.prompt:
Exit Ticket

A youth group has a yard sale to raise money for a charity. The group earns $800 but decides to put its money in the bank for a while. Calculate the amount of money the group will have given the following scenarios:

Cool Bank pays simple interest at a rate of 4%, and the youth group leaves the money in for 3 years.

Hot Bank pays an interest rate of 3% compounded annually, and the youth group leaves the money in for 5 years.

If the youth group needs the money quickly, which is the better choice? Why?
exitTicket.solution:
A youth group has a yard sale to raise money for a charity. The group earns $800 but decides to put its money in the bank for a while. Calculate the amount of money the group will have given the following scenarios:

Cool Bank pays simple interest at a rate of 4%, and the youth group leaves the money in for 3 years.

$800(0.04)(3)=$96 interest earned

$896 total

Hot Bank pays an interest rate of 3% compounded annually, and the youth group leaves the money in for 5 years.

$800(1.03)^{5}=$927.42

If the youth group needs the money quickly, which is the better choice? Why?

If the youth group needs the money quickly, it should use Cool Bank since that bank pays a higher rate than Hot Bank. The lower rate is better for a longer period of time due to the compounding interest.

problems.prompt: $250 is invested at a bank that pays 7% simple interest. Calculate the amount of money in the account after 1 year, 3 years, 7 years, and 20 years.
problems.solution:
$267.50, $302.50, $372.50, $600.00

$325 is borrowed from a bank that charges 4% interest compounded annually. How much is owed after 1 year, 3 years, 7 years, 20 years?

$338.00, $365.58, $427.68, $712.12

problems.prompt: Joseph has $10,000 to invest. He can go to Yankee Bank that pays 5% simple interest or Met Bank that pays 4% interest compounded annually. At how many years will Met Bank be the better choice?
problems.solution: At 12 years, Met Bank is a better choice.
